title: Victoria Harbour, Hong Kong, China
caption: The only way is up
subtitle: Victoria Harbour, Hong Kong, China
description: Welcome to Hong Kong, home to more skyscrapers than any other city in the world. Those pictured here tower above Victoria Harbour, whose deep waters helped the island develop into a busy trading port. Ships carrying tea, silk and other goods have passed through since the 1840s, but growth accelerated in the decades after the Second World War, fuelling a construction boom. With little flat land available between the harbour and the hills, developers had to build upwards, creating this distinctive skyline. As of 2026, Hong Kong has 569 completed buildings at least 150 metres tall — more than any other city in the world.

title: Frozen azalea with red leaves
caption: Frosty foliage
subtitle: Frost on azalea foliage
description: As autumn's first frost sets in, ice crystals form on the leaves of evergreen shrubs, such as this azalea. The pinks, oranges and yellows of their spring blooms have long since faded, but a new colourful display awaits as their green leaves turn shades of red and purple. For the plants, these pigments can help protect leaves against environmental stresses as temperatures drop. For gardeners, they create a vibrant autumnal display, framed in white frost. When spring arrives, fresh green growth will emerge, and the colourful cycle begins anew.

title: Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument, New Mexico, USA
caption: Built to last
subtitle: Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument, New Mexico
description: Incredible views and rock-solid foundations are part of the charm of these ancient dwellings, set into the cliffside in New Mexico. Nomads had long used the natural caves above Cliff Dweller Creek as temporary shelter, but it was the Native American Mogollon people who made them their home. Archaeologists believe they created dozens of rooms inside five alcoves in the 1270s and 1280s. Up to 15 families lived here at any one time, raising children, making pottery and overlooking the fertile Gila River valley where they grew crops and hunted wildlife. For reasons unknown, the Mogollon people moved on around 1300, leaving behind one of the American Southwest's most important archaeological sites.

title: Trail of the Cedars, Glacier National Park, Montana, USA
caption: Step into the great outdoors
subtitle: Trail of the Cedars, Glacier National Park, Montana, USA
description: Today's image features the Trail of the Cedars, one of 1,126 kilometres of hiking trails in Glacier National Park, Montana. Its 1.4km-long loop includes a raised boardwalk which cuts a path through western red cedars and hemlock trees. The park boasts routes for all abilities, taking in alpine lakes, wildflower meadows, mountain passes and wilderness stretching to the Canadian border.

title: Pair of barn owls
caption: Hunting from dusk till dawn
subtitle: A pair of barn owls at dusk
description:
These barn owls, bathed in the evening light, are waiting for the hunt to begin. As night falls, the birds of prey swoop into action, listening for the faint movements of mice and voles in the grass and leaves. Their heart-shaped faces help funnel sound towards their exceptionally sensitive ears, allowing them to locate prey with remarkable precision in the dark. They then swoop down almost silently, their soft feathers helping to muffle the sound of their approach.
In autumn, young barn owls may begin dispersing from the areas where they were raised to find territories of their own. As the nights grow longer, you might spot them earlier in the evening, gliding over fields in search of supper.

title: The "Body of Knowledge" sculpture by Jaume Plensa at Goethe University in Frankfurt, Germany
caption: Where ideas take shape
subtitle: World Philosophy Day
description:
It's World Philosophy Day, when thinkers come together to explore life's enduring questions. To mark the occasion, today's image features "Body of Knowledge", a sculpture at Goethe University in Frankfurt, Germany. Created by Spanish artist Jaume Plensa, it combines steel letters from eight different alphabets to form a human figure. Plensa explains: 'Our body is the home of the spirit. The place in which ideas live.'
World Philosophy Day encourages us to look beyond easy answers and explore the questions that shape us and the world around us.

title: Diving humpback whale, Kvaloya, Troms, Northern Norway
caption: Feasting in the fjords
subtitle: Diving humpback whale, Kvaloya, Troms, Northern Norway
description: Off the coast of Kvaløya in Troms, northern Norway, humpback whales move through the cold Arctic waters in search of a proper feast. They visit the region in winter, following migrating herring into the fjords. Humpbacks are known for their remarkable feeding techniques, including bubble-net feeding, in which some whales blow rings or walls of bubbles to corral fish before surging upwards with their mouths open to catch their prey. In today's image, a humpback slips beneath the icy waves under a glowing pastel sky, capturing a moment of tranquillity in Norway's wild north.

title: Nice, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France
caption: Terracotta dreams
description: Bathed in a sun-kissed glow, Nice is a patchwork of terracotta rooftops, historic churches and pastel façades along the French Riviera, as seen in today's image. Founded by the ancient Greeks and long associated with the Italian House of Savoy, Nice officially became part of France in 1860. Today, its layered past remains visible throughout this coastal city in the south of France, where historic architecture meets the blue waters of the Mediterranean and the sunlit hills of the Côte d'Azur.
